subject: Invoice delivery: signed PDF vs portal upload — Harvest Health
messages:
From: Sarah Jennings <accounts.payable@harvesthealth.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ap@harvesthealth.com
Date: 2028-04-20T09:16:00Z
Subject: Invoice delivery preference and metadata

Hi Chloe,

Quick question from our AP team as we set up Redwood as a new vendor. Do you push invoices into a vendor portal (SFTP / API / peppol) or will we receive signed PDF invoices via email? Our procurement folks prefer portal integration for automated matching, but compliance needs a one-time signed invoice for our onboarding audit.

If email is the only option, can you confirm:
- whether the PDFs will include a visible VAT number and reverse-charge flag where applicable
- what filename pattern you use (we need YYYYMMDD_Invoice_CompanyName.pdf)
- whether you can include our PO number on the invoice and in the invoice metadata for automated matching

I've attached our Harvest invoice template and our onboarding checklist (see attachment stub: Harvest_Invoice_Template.xlsx).

Thanks — the sooner we lock this down the sooner we can get you into our payment run.

Best,
Sarah Jennings
Senior AP Analyst
Harvest Health
accounts.payable@harvesthealth.com

Attachment: Harvest_Invoice_Template.xlsx (stub)

From: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Jennings <accounts.payable@harvesthealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-04-20T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Invoice delivery preference and metadata

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers up front: we support both portal/API push and emailed PDFs, and we can provide a one-time signed PDF for your audit. For automated AP matching we recommend the portal/API route (fewer manual steps).

Details:
- Portal/API: we can push invoices to an SFTP endpoint or via our webhook push. We also support Peppol for EU entities — happy to enable that if your system supports it. When you opt for portal/API we include structured metadata (PO number, VAT id, invoice_type, and custom tags) so matching is reliable.
- Email PDFs: if you prefer email we can send password-protected PDFs or signed PDFs. Filenames: we can adopt the YYYYMMDD_Invoice_HarvestHealth.pdf pattern; nested entity suffixes are possible.
- VAT and reverse-charge: we will render the VAT ID and the reverse-charge statement when applicable. If you need a separate VAT breakdown line for each tax jurisdiction, note that requires our billing entity mapping (we have separate legal entities for EU/UK).

Action items for us to move forward: please confirm the channel you prefer (Portal/API/SFTP/Peppol or Email), and provide:
1) billing contact name & email for our onboarding (person who will accept the first signed invoice)
2) the PO numbering convention you use (will you supply PO on each invoice?)
3) desired filename pattern confirmation

I'll attach an internal example showing how we embed PO and VAT fields (attachment stub: redwood_signed-invoice-sample.pdf).

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0146

Attachment: redwood_signed-invoice-sample.pdf (stub)

From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Jennings <accounts.payable@harvesthealth.com>, chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-04-21T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Invoice delivery preference and metadata

Looping in to confirm commercial/ops side. Per our Master Services Agreement (section 4.2) we can accept either channel; for recurring monthly billing we prefer portal/API because it avoids manual remittance delays and reduces failed-match cases by >70% in our metrics. That said, we can provide the one-time signed PDF you need for onboarding.

For Harvest onboarding I'd suggest:
- Step 1: provide billing contact and PO convention (Harvest) — we will send one signed PDF to the onboarding contact for your audit record.
- Step 2: enable webhook push (our side) to your SFTP or provide a Peppol receiver ID if you want e-invoicing.
- Step 3: after the first signed invoice we flip to portal/API for ongoing invoices. We keep an email copy (CC) for your AP team for 60 days by default.

If legal requires a hand-signed invoice rather than a digitally signed PDF, tell us and we can also generate a scanned, wet-signed copy (expedite with DocuSign for standard countersign).

If you confirm portal + PO on every invoice we can also include a machine-readable XML payload alongside each PDF to speed matching.

—Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

P.S. tagging @kimberly.park for VAT/finance confirmation on entity mapping and EU reverse-charge handling.

From: Sarah Jennings <accounts.payable@harvesthealth.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ap@harvesthealth.com
Date: 2028-04-22T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Invoice delivery preference and metadata

Thanks Chloe and Ben — appreciate the options and the clear plan. We will:
1) Opt into SFTP push for on-going invoices (Harvest will provide SFTP credentials by Friday).
2) Please send the one-time signed PDF to me (Sarah Jennings) for our onboarding packet — filename should follow YYYYMMDD_Invoice_HarvestHealth.pdf.
3) PO convention: we will provide a PO on every invoice in the format HARV-YYYY-#### (we'll include an example in the SFTP credentials email).
4) VAT: Harvest is EU-registered (VAT ID: GB999888777). Reverse-charge applies — please include the standard EU reverse-charge statement and the VAT ID on the invoice and in the machine-readable metadata.

Attached: harvest_signed-approval-stub.pdf (we'll include the completed onboarding checklist in the SFTP creds email).

If you can produce the one signed PDF by end of day Monday it will get us through finance sign-off and onto the first payment run.

Best regards,
Sarah Jennings
Senior AP Analyst
Harvest Health
accounts.payable@harvesthealth.com

Attachment: harvest_signed-approval-stub.pdf (stub)
